dates.notes: Signed at Dushanbe on 28 September 2018 by the CIS Heads of State. Article 17 provides that the Agreement enters into force 30 days after the depositary receives the third notification of completion of domestic procedures; it entered into force on 12 March 2020. For Russia it entered into force on 17 July 2022 after ratification. Article 17(2) terminates the 2001 CIS Agreement on computer information crimes in relations between the States that become parties to this Agreement.

legal_nature.rationale: An agreement adopted by the CIS Heads of State, subject to domestic procedures and notified to the depositary, with entry into force after the third notification. It creates binding obligations for the Parties and is a treaty, not a political declaration.

parties.note: Seven States are listed as Parties in the Russian legal register: Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan. The CIS depositary page does not display a current party table; the total is therefore declared, not verified against an itemised depositary record.

ratifications.note: The Agreement uses notification of completion of domestic procedures rather than a separate ratification tally. Russia's ratification is documented, but no complete ratification count is asserted.

reservations: Russia made a reservation on 14 June 2022 concerning the treatment of certain offences under Article 3(1)(g), (d), (zh) and (z) as criminal or administrative offences.

cyber_provisions: Cooperation among the competent authorities of the Parties on preventing, detecting, suppressing, disclosing and investigating information-technology crimes.
Forms of cooperation, requests for assistance, confidentiality and data protection, and the procedure for executing requests.
A list of information-technology offences in Article 3, including unlawful access, interception, interference, data modification and the use of malicious programs.
Accession by CIS member States after entry into force and termination of the 2001 computer-information agreement between Parties.
relevance.excluded_scope: A regional cooperation and criminal-law agreement. It creates no AI-specific obligation and does not establish a supranational regulator.
relevance.reason: The 2018 CIS Agreement is the current regional cybercrime instrument in the post-Soviet space and replaces the 2001 computer-information agreement. It had been missing from the corpus even though it is binding and in force; its absence made the cybercrime layer look more Budapest-centred than it is.
